prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1166; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the roadway in Baytown, Texas, waiting for traffic ahead to clear, when Driver 2 approached from behind and failed to stop in time, striking the rear of Driver 1's vehicle. A Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred just as described by Driver 1, and two independent witnesses at the scene gave consistent accounts. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear bumper and trunk area of Driver 1's vehicle that is consistent with the force of a rear impact of this type. Driver 1 reported pain in the lower back immediately after the crash, and the nature and force of the collision are consistent with that complaint. Officers confirmed through witness statements and on-scene observation that Driver 1 was in the vehicle when the collision occurred. Officers found no indication of prior damage to the vehicle in the same area. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle. Driver 1 was transported for evaluation and the report is submitted for review.
